question.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=1 \\ -2{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=-1 \\ 3{x}_{1}-6{x}_{2}=2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $14a+\frac{b}{c}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 4 \\ 3 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}14 & -28 \\ -28 & 56\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -18\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}14 & -28 & 9 \\ -28 & 56 & -18\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}14 & -28 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{9}{14}+2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{14}+2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{14} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
14a+\frac{b}{c}=14\cdot \frac{9}{14}+\frac{2}{1}=11.
$$
